x: Any one of John Boardman, Douglas Jardine, John Kelly, Lionel Mann (no '20' the week before!) could get under 1 minute 55 secs. and then improve, while the "veteran" track captain isn't giving up yet!

The 800 metres was an uneven race, only settled down the straight, where Peter Hilliar held off a fast-finishing John Boardman. The first five finishers were within 0.8 second of each other, giving an indication of their closeness.

However, our best moment came in the medley relay, where we led all the way until the last 50 yards, where John Boardman was overhauled by Barrington of Poly, despite having run his leg in under 1:58.0.

800m: John Boardman beat his best by nearly 2 seconds, but could only finish 9th, such was the standard. 1500m: John Thresher did a 56 second last lap, but so unfortunately did the winner Thomas (HHH), who was 10 yards up at the bell.

I think we could at last have some strength in depth in the future in what has been our "Cinderella" event since the retirement of Dave Cocks; through such competitors as Mel Ford (around 1-56 relay), John Boardman, John Kelly and Doug Jardine.
We also Have John Boardman, Mel Ford and another junior, John Stowe, under the 2 minute barrier and Colin Pearson and John Kelly should also be shortly.

Other useful performances came from Steve White, Peter Carton, John Boardman, Adrian Major, Bill Kerr, Lee Sullivan and Glyn Ratcliffe. One can say that it was a good team effort, but just wait and see what we can do at Wimbledon Park!
They have numerous runners to back them up notably JOHN BOARDMAN BILL CURTIN, DOUGLAS JARDINE, JOHN KELLY, and LIONEL MANN - training for a fast finishing marathon.
Steve White chalked up yet another sprint double, and Bill Kerr took the 1500m., while Jim Rimmer (3rd in 1m. 57.5s.) and John Boardman (fourth in 1m. 58s.) can be said to have run well in the 800m.
Open Meeting at Crystal Palace on February 12th, the 3000 metres gave John Boardman and Doug Maughan the chance to show their early season paces.
